metaData.originalTitle: Sea's View on the Future of Agentic Software Development with Codex
metaData.title: Sea's View on the Future of Agentic Software Development with Codex
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Sea Co-Founder David Chen discusses how rolling out OpenAI's Codex across the organization is shifting software development from productivity gains to a fundamental reconfiguration of engineering teams, with developers evolving into system orchestrators.
metaData.summary: In this interview from OpenAI's Executive Function series, David Chen, Co-Founder of Sea and CPO of Shopee, explains the strategic rationale behind deploying Codex across Sea's entire development organization. He describes how Codex goes beyond autocomplete to provide deep contextual awareness of Sea's massive microservices architecture, reducing the cognitive load of tracing dependencies and understanding legacy logic. Internal data shows 87% weekly active users among developers, with 73% of high-raters recommending it to colleagues. Chen emphasizes that AI agents are increasingly operating within CI/CD pipelines, reasoning through product requirements and autonomously proposing implementations. He argues that Southeast Asia is uniquely positioned as a proving ground for AI-native development due to its complex, multilingual, fragmented markets. Looking ahead, Chen predicts a fundamental reconfiguring of engineering teams where developers evolve into system orchestrators focused on product judgment and system design, while AI agents handle operational execution. He also discusses Sea's partnership with OpenAI to host a regional Codex Hackathon Series across Asia to democratize access to advanced AI tools and build a compounding AI-native talent ecosystem.

mainPoints.point: Codex provides deep contextual awareness of large, disparate codebases, reducing friction in navigating microservices architectures.
mainPoints.explanation: In Sea's massive microservices environment, the primary challenge is not typing syntax but tracing dependencies and understanding legacy logic. Codex acts as a localized knowledge engine, allowing engineers to shift cognitive load to higher-level tasks like architectural design.

mainPoints.point: Developers are using Codex to 'think better', not just type faster, with AI agents operating within CI/CD pipelines.
mainPoints.explanation: Sea is transitioning from passive autocomplete to integrated agentic workflows where AI agents reason through product requirements, propose test-driven implementations, surface edge cases, and accelerate debugging loops.

mainPoints.point: AI-assisted development drives engineering discipline by enabling rapid prototyping and exhaustive test coverage.
mainPoints.explanation: By allowing AI to rapidly prototype alternative implementations and generate comprehensive tests, Sea is moving faster while systematically paying down technical debt and shipping more resilient systems.

mainPoints.point: Southeast Asia is uniquely positioned as a proving ground for AI-native software development.
mainPoints.explanation: The region's developers must solve highly complex, multilingual problems across fragmented commerce, payment, logistics, and communication networks, making it an ideal environment for AI-native development.

mainPoints.point: Engineering teams will reconfigure as developers evolve into system orchestrators focused on product judgment and system design.
mainPoints.explanation: As AI agents abstract away the implementation layer, developers will spend the majority of their time on higher-level tasks, with development cycles becoming more iterative and continuous as experimentation costs fall.

keyQuotes: Agentic AI coding tools like Codex are not just about improving localised productivity. They represent a structural multiplier that can help our engineering organisation ramp up speed, responsiveness, and effectiveness amid an increasingly complex operating environment.
The most profound shift is realizing our developers are using Codex to 'think better', not just type faster.
We are actively transitioning from using AI as a passive autocomplete mechanism to integrated agentic workflows.
The winners will be those who relentlessly redesign their engineering culture and workflows around human-AI collaboration today, rather than bolting it onto legacy processes tomorrow.
By upskilling the region's developers today, we are collectively accelerating Southeast Asia's trajectory as a global hub for AI-driven innovation.
